=== Protest Letter Bell County East – Big Hill 765kV Transmission Line.pdf ===
TO: Public Utility Commission of Texas
FROM: Colleen Crenwelge
DATE: June 24, 2026
RE: Docket #59475, Bell County East – Big Hill 765kV Transmission Line

To Whom It May Concern:

My parents, Atlee and Susan Crenwelge, have owned and leased property in Schleicher and
Menard Counties since 2000. They chose property that they knew would support a cow-calf
operation, and they have spent the last 25 years building a successful business and making
improvements (i.e., fencing, wells, vegetation management, etc.). They have also built a small
cabin on the property for their use, and they and others hunt on the property.

The proposed R2 segment of the Bell County East – Big Hill line would affect my parents’
property (tracts #150-153, 521, 522). My parents have many concerns about the proposed
route.

First, it appears the proposed route would bisect my parents’ property, splitting their 1,300+ acre
ranch. Running through the middle of the property instead of along property lines would inflict
the most damage. The proposed route would also be close to existing structures: my parents’
cabin and a hunting camp. Again, this would happen because the route would run through the
middle of the property instead of along property lines.

The 200-ft right of way through the property would create substantial loss of use. The land is
used for ranching and recreational purposes, all of which would be significantly compromised by
transmission infrastructure:
    • Fragmentation of usable acreage
    • Disruption of livestock movement and fencing layout (negatively affecting the rotational
       grazing that my parents are considering)
    • Interference with long-term operational planning
    • Limitation of future building sites and improvements.
Routing alternatives would avoid this multi-parcel disruption.

In addition, my parents are concerned about the impact of noise pollution on livestock and
hunting. They also anticipate that transmission infrastructure would decrease property value and
make the land less appealing to future buyers should they ever need to sell.

Finally, my parents agree with other commenters who have questioned 1) whether the proposed
routes make sufficient use of existing rights-of-way to mitigate negative community and
environmental effects; 2) whether all alternative energy sources have been explored; and 3)
whether enough is known about the potential health effects of 765kV transmission lines.

My parents would urge the prioritization of existing transportation corridors, such as U.S. and
state highway rights-of-way, and property lines to minimize new disturbance.

Thank you for your attention to these comments.
